      <title>Enzo Maresca rues Manchester City’s lack of desire after defeat at Nottingham Forest</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/07/enzo-maresca-nottingham-forest-manchester-city-premier-league</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>‘You need desire and intensity … we didn’t match them’</p></li><li><p>City have now lost three successive league matches</p></li></ul><p>Enzo Maresca blamed his side’s lack of desire and the way they were outgunned in duels for a third successive Premier League defeat. After winning their first seven games of the season, <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/07/nottingham-forest-manchester-city-premier-league-match-report">Manchester City’s 3-1 loss at Nottingham Forest</a> extended their poor run.</p><p>Jair Cunha dispossessed Josko Gvardiol to score the opener, then Liam Delap struck twice with muscular surges on the break as Forest won their first home league game since April. “Today I think [the problem] has been general,” said Maresca. “It’s not about one player. In the first half we lost all the duels, all the contacts. Against this team, that is fighting relegation, if you don’t match them … it’s something we need to understand. In this kind of game, if you’re not able to win duels and second balls like in the first half, you struggle.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/07/enzo-maresca-nottingham-forest-manchester-city-premier-league">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Delap’s Nottingham Forest stunners hand Manchester City third league defeat in a row</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/07/nottingham-forest-manchester-city-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>Wait long enough and results will come to reflect performances. Manchester City may have won their first seven league games of the season but they always looked vulnerable, and now have lost three in a row. Nottingham Forest may have been second bottom but, other than the twin curses of missing chances and giving away daft goals, they seemed to be playing reasonably well. Put the two together and the outcome was a dramatic regression to the mean. It turns out the stats were right, after all.</p><p>Liam Delap scored twice to remind people just what a good striker he can be. Oliver Glasner, <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/31/brentford-nottingham-forest-premier-league-match-report">after last week’s anger</a>, can breathe a little easier in his job. And Enzo Maresca remains a paradox, a manager obsessive about control whose teams always seem oddly susceptible to direct running.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/07/nottingham-forest-manchester-city-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Martin Ødegaard extends Arsenal lead at top with winner to break Hull resistance</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/07/arsenal-hull-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>As most Arsenal supporters would testify, patience is a virtue. They needed plenty during the 22-year wait <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/may/19/arsenal-premier-league-champions-manchester-city-bournemouth">to be crowned Premier League champions</a> and Mikel Arteta’s side certainly had to retain their composure as they tried to break down a dogged Hull side. They had not beaten Arsenal in 14 attempts since winning on their first visit to this ground in 2008. But with 20 minutes to play, there was still every chance that Sergej Jakirovic’s team could have pulled off one of the shocks of the season.</p><p>Arsenal had already been denied a penalty just before half-time for a shirt pull on Kai Havertz in the box a week after escaping <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/01/liverpool-arsenal-premier-league-match-report">the same crime against Liverpool</a> at Anfield, in a moment of controversy that could have been the major talking point from this match. Martin Ødegaard had other ideas and the Arsenal captain’s fifth goal of the season was enough to ensure they will go into the international break with a healthy lead over Manchester City. Enzo Maresca’s side are up next here in the league after the international break, with Arsenal having matched their record tally of 27 points from their opening 10 games. The signs look ominous for the rest, even if they were made to work for the points throughout by their opponents.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/07/arsenal-hull-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>
